$comment: #EXP-2024: the live view of an agent's space on Exponential Desktop (f5-f6-design.md section 6 on #EXP-1514), a pure projection replayed in TS (src/spaces.ts) and Rust (uicore-model spaces.rs); the shell feeds it as `/spaces` (the taskbar's Agent spaces button and its list) and `/spaceView` (the pinned view). ROWS (`spaceRows(spaces, sessions) -> [{id, session, number, title, subtitle}]`, the `rows` cases {name, spaces, sessions, expected}): `spaces` = the compositor's ListSpaces ({id, session}: a space's id is `space-<n>`, n its number, counted up and never reused; `session` = the session its grant names), `sessions` = the session rows the shell's signed-in accounts hold ({id, title, parentId, rootId}, the title already resolved the way every client resolves it). One row per space in the order of the NUMBERS (`space-2` before `space-10`; an id without a number after the numbered ones, by id). `number` = n (1 to 15 digits), null without one (or with more). `title` = its session's title, trimmed of white space (Unicode's White_Space and JavaScript's, U+FEFF and U+0085 too); a session no account holds (another account's, a teammate's private one on a shared device, a space made by hand), or an empty title = `copy.untitled` with {n} = the number (the whole id without one). `subtitle` = a child session's chat (parentId set): its root's title (rootId, trimmed), null for a root session, for a root no account holds and for an empty one. NO state word (the product's Working outlives a dead host; the picture is the state). The count (the button shows while it is above 0) = the number of spaces. VIEW (`spaceView(space, display, large) -> {width, height, picture: {width, height}, pixels: {width, height}, large, canGrow}`, the `view` cases {name, space, display, large, expected}): the pinned view is a box at the bottom right of the FIRST display above the taskbar: inside a `constants.border` px border, `constants.header` px of header (the title, the size and the close button) over the picture. `space` = the space's output size {width, height}; `display` = the first display's logical size and scale {width, height, scale}. The picture's width = min(`constants.maxWidth`, floor(display width / 3)); `large` asks for twice that, granted only where it fits (canGrow): the box at twice the width within display width - 2 x shell-layout.json panelMargin, and its height within display height - taskbarHeight - 2 x panelMargin. A box that does not fit that height is narrowed until it does (floor). The picture's height = round(width x space height / space width) (the space's aspect; a space of no size = 16:10); the box (`width`, `height`, the layer's size) = the picture + 2 x border wide, header + picture + 2 x border tall. `pixels` = the picture's box times the display's scale, rounded: what the capture is shrunk to, so the picture stays sharp at 1.5 and 2 (never bigger than the space itself: the shrink never scales up).

rows.name: a session's title, trimmed; a root session has no second line
a child session's chat is the second line
a child whose root no account holds has no second line
a session no account holds: Agent space n
an empty title: Agent space n
the order of the numbers, not of the ids; an id without a number last
two spaces of one tree: each row its own session, both under the chat
white space either twin knows is trimmed: a pasted byte-order mark is no title
a number of more than 15 digits is no number

view.name: a 1280-wide display: a third of it
scale 1.5: the picture's pixels are the box times the scale
large where it fits: twice the width
large where it does not fit: the default size
large at scale 2: twice the width, its pixels never above the space
a tall space on a short display is narrowed to fit the height
the pixels never exceed the space
